correctness.rationale: The finite identities are exact: a canonical sign kernel with zero conditional means gives the clockwise-tournament writhe and the first-order inversion projection; their covariance is -(m-1)^2/24. In the mixed fourth-moment expansion only two edges sharing one vertex with the linear factors on their outer endpoints survive at order m^5; the contraction integrals are 1/45 and 1/12, giving 1/1080. The bounded canonical kernel yields O(m^4) fourth moments and controls remainders. A finite-rank Hilbert-space CLT establishes the joint first/second Wiener-chaos limit and independently reproduces the same mixed contraction. Exact rational finite checks were replayed for every permutation through odd size 9. The square-correlation constant uses the independently published marginal fourth moment.

originality.rationale: Even-Zohar (arXiv:1511.09469) proves marginal writhe laws and moment asymptotics, not the stated same-permutation mixed fourth moment. Janson (arXiv:2510.12480, Section 9.1) supplies general cyclic U-statistic methods but explicitly leaves joint extensions to the reader and does not state this mixed-square coefficient. The exact coefficient 1/1080 and consequent nonindependence are not implied by separate marginal convergence or vanishing Pearson correlation. Subject-specific and broader equivalent searches found no explicit dominating primary statement; priority risk remains for unlocated earlier mixed-moment analyses.
residual_risks: A historical mixed-moment calculation may exist under graphical inversions, circular rank measures, or equivalent bi-alternating inversion terminology.
Foata--Zeilberger (1996) full original article was not inspected, although its accessible scope does not suggest the claimed joint asymptotic dependence.
Janson (2025) provides a general route to such calculations; the precise constant could be an unrecorded corollary or appear in other unpublished work.

value.rationale: Writhe and ordinary inversions are natural circular and linear rank-order metrics, and their vanishing correlation makes asymptotic independence a motivated scientific question. The explicit strictly positive mixed-square covariance disproves that conclusion at the first even nonlinear order, identifies the first/second Gaussian-chaos coupling, and yields the nonzero limiting square correlation sqrt(35)/70. This gives a meaningful structural dependence diagnostic, not a routine marginal moment or a renamed statistic.
